Subject: Marketplace commission split and billing terms for private offers (BlueWave)

Hannah — thanks again for the demo last week. We got internal approval to move forward with private offers on AWS and Azure, and are evaluating GCP as an additional channel. Before we sign, procurement asked for clarity on a few items so our finance team can reconcile forecasts across marketplaces:

- Requested rev-share: BlueWave is proposing an 18% rev-share to Redwood on all billed usage for the first 12 months (AWS + Azure + GCP)
- Billing cadence: BlueWave prefers Net60 for marketplace settlements
- Marketplace fees: we need confirmation who absorbs listing/marketplace fees and if they’ll be deducted pre- or post-rev-share

Attached our formal PO and a short summary. Can you confirm Redwood’s acceptance or provide an alternate term sheet? We’d like to close by 2027-11-10 to meet our Q4 onboarding calendar.

Attachments: BlueWave_PO.pdf

Thanks,
Emily Jones

Subject: Re: Marketplace commission split and billing terms for private offers (BlueWave)

Emily — appreciate the clear ask and the PO. High-level response below; forwarding to Finance/Legal for final numbers and exec approval where needed.

- Rev-share: we can be flexible for a pilot. Proposed counter: 20% for AWS and Azure for the first 12 months, with a decaying scale to 15% after year 1 if usage thresholds are met. GCP historically has higher take-rates; tentatively we’d need 22% there unless GA marketplace economics change.
- Billing cadence: Redwood standard is Net30 for marketplace settlements because marketplaces remit differently; Net60 materially increases our working capital burden. We can make an exception to Net45 for the first 12 months if exec approves.
- Marketplace fees: marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP) charge platform fees; our preference is to handle rev-share post-marketplace deductions (i.e., net of marketplace fees). If BlueWave prefers gross, we need a fee offset or higher rev-share to compensate.

I’m attaching a cleaned version of our proposal with the above reflected for internal review. Karthik — can you please loop in Marcus and Laura for finance/legal and prepare an exec approval packet?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Marketplaces

Hannah / team — dropping in a short summary we can present to execs:

Summary for exec packet (short bullet version):
- Account: BlueWave Analytics (DEAL-7231-BW)
- Ask: Approve one-time exception to standard marketplace economics to close private offers across AWS, Azure, and GCP by 2027-11-10
- Proposed terms: AWS/Azure 20% rev-share (first 12 months), GCP 22% (first 12 months); ramp to 15% after year 1 conditional on usage tiers; billing Net45 for first 12 months; clause: rev-share calculated net of marketplace fees
- Rationale: Accelerates revenue recognition in Q4, strategic reference customer for retail analytics vertical; expected incremental ARR of ~$1.5M over 12 months (see finance model)
- Risks: Working capital exposure from Net45/Net60; potential margin compression if marketplaces increase fees; precedence for future marketplace asks
- Decision requested: Exec sign-off (CRO/CFO) or delegated approval to Finance with a hard cap on total subsidy (max $200k first-year impact)

Team — I ran the initial model and attached the workbook. Key notes:

- Base case (BlueWave meets conservative adoption): projected billed usage $7.5M in 12 months; gross to Redwood before marketplace fees ~ $1.35M
- If rev-share is 20% (AWS/Azure) and 22% (GCP) net of marketplace fees, Redwood net revenue impact in year 1 = ~$1.05M; incremental gross subsidy (cash flow deferral) from moving to Net45 = ~$210k in working capital needs
- Recommendation: Approve the proposed differentiated rates (20%/20%/22%) for 12 months, require Net45 (not Net60), and include explicit language that rev-share is calculated net of marketplace platform fees. Also add a 6-month review clause to evaluate economics and change the ramp if needed.
- Approval authority: This exceeds delegated finance approval cap for marketplace concessions — needs CFO (Markus Klein) sign-off. If approved, Finance will track subsidy as a one-off sales incentive and cap total exposure to $225k.

Attachment: finance_impact_model.xlsx
